newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler sees 1997 capital spending increase.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler sees 1997 capital spending increase.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. expects to increase its capital spending in 1997 by about five to 10 percent over the $4.6 billion it spent in 1996, the automaker's chief financial officer said Tuesday.
Gary Valade told reporters in a conference call that Chrysler's 1997 capital expenditures will likely be between the 1996 level and around $5 billion.

Chrysler Chairman Chief Executive Officer Robert Eaton also said the company expected to save about $20 million in annual interest costs associated with the retirement of about $550 million in debt during the fourth quarter.

The debt, which represents half of a debt issue due in 2020, was retired at a cost of $859 million, and will be refinanced later in the first quarter, Valade said. He added that Chrysler will consider refinancing the remainder of the Auburn Hills Trust Guaranteed Exchangeable Certificates sometime in the future.

Eaton said 1997 "should be an excellent year" for the U.S. auto industry. He added that Chrysler currently estimates that U.S. auto industry sales should reach 15.2 million vehicles in 1997, including medium and heavy trucks, compared with 15.4 million in 1996.

Valade also said Chrysler's pension fund for U.S. hourly workers is currently overfunded by $1.4 billion, largely because of favorable changes in interest rates and strong performance of stock market investments during the fourth quarter.
He also said Chrysler is considering adding a third production shift at its Eurostar plant in Graz, Austria, which produces Chrysler minivan models.
